text:
ryan: quick check — i'm about to open a tiny terraform PR to rotate the KMS key we use for the payments secret syncer. main change is a kms_grant for the IRSA role + a small policy tweak. can someone sanity-check ordering and the grant principal/constraints? will push in ~10m.

sofia: :eyes: quick q — is this the syncer running in kube-system that reads secrets from central bucket and writes to namespace-specific k8s secrets? if so the grantee principal should be the assumed-role arn (IRSA) not the service account name.

ryan: yep that's the one. plan: keep controller in kube-system, leave controller SA alone, but add grant to key with grantee_principal = data.aws_iam_role.irsa_payments.arn. also adding an encryption context constraint to limit to namespace=payments. snippet below — feedback welcome.

ryan: ```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "payments_irsa" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.secrets.id
  grantee_principal = data.aws_iam_role.irsa_payments.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "Encrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]

  constraints {
    encryption_context_subset = {
      "namespace" = "payments"
    }
  }
}
```

tara: couple things — (1) grants are eventually consistent; if TF creates grant after the role is assumed it can fail for short windows. we usually do: create role, attach policy, then grant. (2) confirm the encryption_context key you're using: recommend using `aws:EncryptionContext:namespace` or match whatever your secrets-propagator sets.

sofia: +1 on ordering. also note: some controllers use `kms:ViaService` or session tags instead of encryption context. which does the syncer rely on?

ryan: the syncer adds a tag on GenerateDataKey/Encrypt calls like {"namespace":"payments"} so EC subset should work. i'll mirror that. i'll also add depends_on to force role/policy -> grant ordering in TF. example: `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa_payments_attach]`

ashley: small nit — KMS encryption context keys are case-sensitive. the propagator currently sets `namespace` lowercase, so that's fine. also make sure the grant operations include `GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext` if you use that API. otherwise looks ok. :+1:

ryan: good catch, adding GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext. updating snippet.

ryan: ```hcl
operations = [
  "Decrypt",
  "Encrypt",
  "GenerateDataKey",
  "GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext",
]
```

infra-bot: terraform plan for branch `payments/kms-rotate` finished — link: https://ci.internal/redwood/plan/3487 — plan shows aws_kms_grant created after aws_iam_role_policy_attachment (good) but also shows a replace on aws_kms_key.secrets due to description change (watch rotation).

tara: can you paste the specific plan lines for the grant + role? small chance TF will reorder if there are implicit deps.

ryan: plan excerpt: ```
+ aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa_payments_attach
+ aws_kms_grant.payments_irsa
```

ryan: i added explicit depends_on on the grant resource to be safe. testing locally then pushing.

sofia: one more thing — when you rotate the key make sure secrets-propagator has access to old key for decrypting existing secrets (unless you re-encrypt). probably need a staged rotation: add new key, update controller to write new secrets under new key, retire old key after backfill.

ashley: correct. if you rotate KMS key id in-place you'll break decrypt unless you rewrap. staged rotation is safer.

ryan: noted. for this PR i'm not rotating the key material; just updating grant + policy so the IRSA role has explicit decrypt rights and the enc ctx constraint. rotation will be a follow-up that we do staged.

tara: LGTM then. @ashley mind doing quick PR review once it's up?

ashley: will do, ping me when PR link is up. :thumbsup:

ryan: thanks all — pushing PR now, will drop link in thread. :rocket:
